cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg27.txt <<'EOF'
fix(streams): file_put_contents() could not write to a user wrapper, and scandir owned its wording

php-src has ONE opener. `file_put_contents` is `php_stream_open_wrapper` followed by a write, which
is what makes a registered wrapper writable at all. elephc's lowering knew `phar://` and
`compress.zlib://` and sent every other URL to a one-shot filesystem writer, which took `uww://x`
for a FILENAME and answered false with php's "No such file or directory" — while
`file_get_contents()` on the identical URL read it, because the READ side already delegated.

What blocked the write side had nothing to do with wrappers. `LiteralOpenMode` could spell
"whatever the call's `$mode` argument says" or "read-only", and nothing else: a caller with no
`$mode` argument of its own that needs to WRITE had no way to say so. `ReadOnly` was never a kind
— it is the fixed mode `"r"` — so it becomes `Fixed(&'static str)`, seven mechanical call sites,
and `file_put_contents` names `"w"`, or `"a"` when it was passed `FILE_APPEND`.

The route is the one `compress.zlib://` already takes minus the deflate tail, and it reports php's
count: the INPUT byte length, not whatever `stream_write()` claims to have consumed.

`scandir("")` carries php's OWN wording. The openers print the bare `Path must not be empty`;
`scandir()` prints `scandir(): Argument #1 ($directory) must not be empty` — MEASURED. Same guard,
different text, so the constant is its own rather than the shared one being reused for something
it does not say.

The read/write surface of a user wrapper is now complete: `fread`, `fgets`, `fgetc`,
`stream_get_contents`, `stream_get_line`, `file_get_contents`, `file`, `readfile`, `fpassthru` and
`file_put_contents` all reach it, verified against `php -n` 8.5.6.
EOF
